scope: Identity-only correspondence between two left-front BANC motor neurons and the two fast femur-tibia FlyMimic muscle labels; no neural timing or excitation transfer.

provenance.bancSource: BANC v888 public Lee Lab compiled tables
provenance.flyMimicPaper: Özdil et al., Musculoskeletal simulation of limb movement biomechanics in Drosophila melanogaster, ICLR 2026

transmitterBoundary.retainedConflict: Both mapped BANC rows carry predicted GABA calls near 0.55 confidence. These metadata are not reinterpreted as inhibitory neuromuscular action and do not determine actuator sign or gain.

excluded.reason: The FlyMimic paper identifies the fast tibia extensor as a dominant force generator; SETi is a distinct slow motor-unit identity and is not substituted for it.
No exact source-supported one-to-one correspondence to a FlyMimic actuator label has been established.

excluded.flyMimicActuatorPattern: all non-tibia and non-fast front-leg MTUs
excluded.reason: Muscle attachment labels alone do not identify a BANC motor neuron or justify a neural gain.

gainBoundary.reason: The 7.0382 µN Azevedo fast-flexor value is an external restrained-probe force at a 417 µm lever, whereas FlyMimic exposes internal actuator/tendon force in a different preparation. Equating them would conflate physical quantities and cannot calibrate spike-to-excitation gain.

promotionRequirements: Direct or independently constrained spike/activation-to-muscle-excitation evidence for the matched preparation.
A preparation-compatible timing transfer and uncertainty model.
Resolution of transmitter/receptor semantics without treating a predicted presynaptic transmitter label as muscle-action sign.
Independent validation against held-out muscle, tendon or joint-load observations.
